clips.hook_line_1: 手写代码 vs AI全包
clips.hook_line_2: DHH两月没敲一行代码
clips.summary_zh: Ruby on Rails 之父 DHH 坦言新项目近两个月 100% 由 AI Agent 编写，人只审核心架构；但百万用户级大型老代码库仍难靠 AI 全自动演进。
clips.en_raw: Almost right from the beginning I'm working on that version, the agent acceleration neared 100%. And in the last 2 months it has been 100%. I have not written really any of the code that shipped in Quattro by hand. I've reviewed the shape of all of it. I've reviewed the individual lines of anything that's critical in the model layer of the system. And I've not looked at the bunch of the UI code. I have not looked at the bunch of the auxiliary code. And I've not written any of the new functionality entirely by hand. But then the web part, actually evolving Basecamp and Hey, our professional products that have lots of users and are relatively large code bases, have proven surprisingly tricky to fully accelerate with agents.

clips.video_title: Anthropic S-1 Shocker, Greatest Business Ever? Google’s $500B Wipeout, Midterm Predictions
clips.hook_line_1: 巨亏800亿 vs 印钞机
clips.hook_line_2: Anthropic招股书真相
clips.summary_zh: All-In 播客拆解 Anthropic 招股书：媒体热炒的 800 亿美元巨亏只是可转债估值飙升带来的账面会计幻影，并非真实烧钱，其资本效率反而惊人。
clips.en_raw: So, number one is that this $80 billion loss number that we've heard so much about, that the media has constantly been pumping and harping on as proof that Anthropic was either a fake business or that we were in this sort of whole bubble, that narrative basically just got completely refuted because it turns out that that $80 billion loss is a phantom number. It resulted from the fact that Anthropic had issued convertible notes to basically their infrastructure partners like Amazon and so forth. And as Anthropic's valuation increased, those convertible notes got recorded as a loss on the balance sheet and that flowed through into the income statement, but it's not a real loss. If they had just issued equity, that loss wouldn't be there. So, it was not a cash loss. It's basically a fake number. And in fact, what was revealed in this S-1 is that Anthropic has been an extraordinarily capital-efficient business.

And as Anthropic's valuation increased, those convertible notes got recorded as a loss on the balance sheet and that flowed through into the income statement, but it's not a real loss. If they had just issued equity, that loss wouldn't be there. So, it was not a cash loss. It's basically a fake number. And in fact, what was revealed in this S-1 is that Anthropic has been an extraordinarily capital-efficient business.
clips.zh_full: 第一大真相，就是外界传得沸沸扬扬的“800亿美元巨亏”，主流媒体一直在疯狂炒作、反复拿它说事，把它当成 Anthropic 是伪商业模式、或者整个 AI 都是泡沫的铁证——仿佛整个行业都在裸泳。但这份招股书直接把这种论调彻底打脸了！因为那 800 亿美元亏损，纯粹是个“账面幻影数字”。它唯一的原因，是 Anthropic 早前发行了可转换债券，发给了亚马逊等算力基础设施战略伙伴。随着 Anthropic 估值暴涨，这些可转债在会计准则下，必须按公允价值变动计提为资产负债表上的“亏损”，进而流进了利润表，但它根本不是真亏钱！如果当初直接发普通股，这笔亏损压根不会存在。所以它一分钱现金都没亏，本质上就是个失真的会计数字。恰恰相反，S-1 招股书真正揭露的是：Anthropic 其实是一家资本效率高到惊人的印钞级生意！

clips.video_title: Inside China's robot revolution | BBC News
clips.hook_line_1: 中国无人工厂 vs 美国
clips.hook_line_2: 200万台机器人三倍碾压
clips.summary_zh: BBC 深入中国全自动汽车产线：中国在役工业机器人已突破 200 万台，规模达美国的 3 倍，全无人化工位正以惊人速度压低智造成本。
clips.en_raw: Facing an aging workforce, a declining population, China is turning to automation. But, millions rely on these factory jobs. So, this shift comes with risks. Here at the final part of the assembly line is where they really do need humans. But, there are more robots working in Chinese factories than anywhere else in the world. 2 million at the last count. That's three times more than in the United States. So, does that mean workers here could eventually be replaced? Fewer workers does mean this car costs less to make. Some of our work stations are already fully automated and require no human involvement. I think the day that all cars in China are made by robots will come very quickly.

clips.video_title: Warren Buffett: The Only 4 Stocks I'd Buy If Markets Crash 50% Tomorrow
clips.hook_line_1: 精准抄底vs买好公司
clips.hook_line_2: 巴菲特70年从不抄底
clips.summary_zh: 巴菲特坦言投资70年从未买在最低点：暴跌40%后再跌10%在长期毫无意义，真正改变命运的是恐慌时敢不敢出手买入好公司。
clips.en_raw: They are the ones who act when everyone else is paralyzed by fear. Let me share something else that most investors get wrong about crash investing. They think they need to catch the exact bottom. They think if they buy when the market is down 40% and it goes down another 10%, they have made a mistake. This is completely backwards thinking. If you buy a wonderful business at a wonderful price, it does not matter if the price goes a little lower after you buy. What matters is where the business will be in 5 years, in 10 years, in 20 years. The difference between buying at the absolute bottom and buying 10% above the bottom is essentially meaningless over long holding periods. But the difference between buying during a crash and not buying at all. That is enormous. That is life-changing. I have never caught the exact bottom of any crash, not once in 70 years of investing.

If you buy a wonderful business at a wonderful price, it does not matter if the price goes a little lower after you buy. What matters is where the business will be in 5 years, in 10 years, in 20 years. clips.video_title: America Needs An Open-Source AI Strategy
clips.hook_line_1: 美国闭源 vs 中国开源
clips.hook_line_2: 全球多数人将用中国模型
clips.summary_zh: CNBC深度警示硅谷闭源路线危机：当OpenAI与谷歌紧锁模型收费时，DeepSeek、智谱与月之暗面正凭免费可定制的开源权重席卷全球开发者生态。
clips.en_raw: Closed AI is what most people know. Open AI's Chat GPT, Anthropic's Claude, Google's Gemini. Their most powerful models, they control the price, the rules, you pay for access. Open weight AI is different. The model can be downloaded, inspected, customized, run on your own infrastructure, and it's often cheaper. China's Deep Seek was a wake-up call. Then Z.ai's latest GLM model, now Moonshot's Kimi K3. China is taking over. They have a dominant share, no question. And the biggest players in American AI, they're now calling for open source AI, too. But Washington's AI strategy is still focused on hardware. Protect the chips, build the data centers, add the power, all while China gains ground in the models the world is increasingly running on. The vast majority of humans on the planet will use Chinese models. Why?
clips.en_clean: Closed AI is what most people know. Open AI's Chat GPT, Anthropic's Claude, Google's Gemini. Their most powerful models, they control the price, the rules, you pay for access. Open weight AI is different. The model can be downloaded, inspected, customized, run on your own infrastructure, and it's often cheaper. China's Deep Seek was a wake-up call. Then Z.ai's latest GLM model, now Moonshot's Kimi K3. China is taking over. They have a dominant share, no question. And the biggest players in American AI, they're now calling for open source AI, too. But Washington's AI strategy is still focused on hardware. Protect the chips, build the data centers, add the power, all while China gains ground in the models the world is increasingly running on. The vast majority of humans on the planet will use Chinese models. Why?
clips.zh_full: 大多数人熟知的AI，都是闭源大模型——比如OpenAI的ChatGPT、Claude以及谷歌Gemini。最强大的模型攥在巨头手里，他们定价格、定规则，你必须交钱才能调用。但开放权重AI彻底不同：模型可以自由下载、审查、深度定制并私有化部署，而且成本往往低得多。中国的DeepSeek敲响了第一记警钟，紧接着是智谱最新GLM模型，如今又是月之暗面Kimi。中国正在接管开源生态，毫无疑问已占据压倒性份额；连美国AI界的巨头们，现在也开始疾呼美国必须发展开源AI。可华盛顿的战略仍死盯硬件：严防芯片、狂建数据中心、拼命补电力，殊不知中国模型正在全球底层应用生态中攻城略地。未来地球上绝大多数人都将运行在中国模型之上——为什么会这样？

clips.en_raw: Semiconductors have become a key part of the tech rivalry between the US and China. Their concerns that an invasion of Taiwan by China could choke off the supply of these cuttingedge chips to the rest of the world and give Beijing control of this essential technology. So, how did Taiwan semiconductor become so dominant? The fundamental technology was actually invented in America and gave Silicon Valley its name as most chips are created with silicon. In the '90s, the US manufactured a third of the world's chips. Today, none of the advanced chips is made in the USA. Companies like Intel used to build and design chips inhouse. But beginning in the 1980s, American firms started struggling against competition from Japanese companies.

clips.video_title: How Huawei Just Built an Impossible Chip
clips.hook_line_1: 光刻受限 vs 架构折叠
clips.hook_line_2: 拆解华为芯片密度突围
clips.summary_zh: 在传统光刻微缩逼近物理极限的背景下，物理学家拆解华为逻辑折叠布线专利：通过垂直折叠高时延信号路径，华为三年内将晶体管密度硬生生提升了23%。
clips.en_raw: During chip layout, you find the signal paths with the tightest timing constraints, the connections actually throttling the chip's overall speed. Then you fold them, so they sit closer together vertically. But what does it actually mean in terms of chip performance? And here I want to talk through some of the numbers that Huawei have presented, and keep in mind we still haven't seen any third-party validation yet. The last generation of the Huawei chip before any of this logic folding implementation taking place is the current chip, and it had a transistor density that sat at around 155 million transistors per square millimeter. It had taken a team a full 3 years from the previous generation of the current chip to get from 126 to this 155 million transistor per square millimeter number. That is a 23% gain over 3 years, which is respectable, but also shows exactly what you'd expect, that geometric scaling with old lithography approaches is kind of hitting a ceiling.

clips.summary_zh: 仅因化学品中混入一丁点异物，台积电就曾被迫报废数万片晶圆、痛失5.5亿美元营收；因此赴美建造亚利桑那4纳米晶圆厂时，唯有像素级复刻台湾产线才能存活。
clips.en_raw: TSMC had to scrap an estimated 10,000 to 30,000 wafers. eating a loss of about $550 million in revenue. One foreign polymer in a chemical, one tiny floor, cascaded into over half a billion dollars of damage. This incident hammered home the point. Vigilance over process consistency isn't paranoia, it's survival. So when TSMC agreed to build an advanced fab in Arizona producing 5 nanometerclass chips later adjusted to 4 nanometers for American customers, they knew the only way to succeed was to copy exact their Taiwan operations. The Arizona FAB, designated FAB 21, would be modeled on TSMC's cuttingedge facilities in Taiwan's Tynan Science Park.

clips.video_title: Value Investing Explained in 5 Levels of Difficulty
clips.hook_line_1: 今天拿百万vs等二十年
clips.hook_line_2: 一分钟看懂DCF估值本质
clips.summary_zh: 今天拿100万还是20年后再拿100万？所有股票估值的底层核心就是现金流折现（DCF）：利率和折现率越高，远期画饼的资产缩水越惨烈。
clips.en_raw: Let me ask you a rhetorical question: Would you rather have $1 million today or $1 million in 20 years? The answer should be quite obvious, not only because money may have more utility for you when you are younger, but also because money can be used to generate more money. It matters not only how much cash flow we receive from our investments, but also when we receive it. The sooner, the more valuable the investment. This is the core of the discounted cashflow (or DCF) analysis where we use a discount rate to reduce the value of future cash flows. If we use a low discount rate, money in the future is worth quite a bit, but if we use a higher one, the value diminishes quickly. After we’ve taken the time value of money into account, we simply sum up these reduced cash flows to see how much the asset is worth today.

clips.summary_zh: 为什么图灵奖得主杨立昆敢拿十亿美元逆势豪赌大语言模型走不通？他断言缺失的核心拼图是理解物理因果的世界模型，唯有它能孕育常识。
clips.en_raw: Shouldn't we figure out what's the what's the secret there? Yeah. And my guess about it is the secret is world models. LeCun's billion-dollar bet is that the missing piece of modern AI is world models. Models that make predictions about the physical world. As he says in his 2022 position paper, common sense can be seen as a collection of models of the world that can tell an agent what is likely, what is plausible, and what is impossible. Using such world models, animals can learn new skills with very few trials. They can predict the consequences of their actions. They can reason, plan, explore, and imagine new solutions to problems. LeCun goes on to argue that joint embedding architectures offer the right foundation to build world models on top of.

clips.hook_line_2: 华尔街漏算的中国AI杀招

clips.en_raw: And it really comes at a time when expensive AI is already eating into budgets. And that is a really hard trade-off for enterprises, for companies, for Fortune 500 to ignore. Agentic AI is only going to intensify those costs. More complex tasks, more steps, more tokens. So, now that Jipu, or also known as Z.ai, is in the picture, Agentic open source, it might be the next big threat out of China. And here's the part of the story, the AI story, that I think Wall Street is still missing here. For the last few years, everyone has been obsessed with these AI leaderboards. Who has the smartest model? Who's the best at coding? Which one is ahead on reasoning? But that is not how companies buy software. Companies are increasingly asking, "What is good enough?" And what does it cost to run this thing a million times or more? All of my employees running it a million times over the course of weeks, months, a year.

clips.video_title: Stop Prompting Claude. Use Karpathy's Method Instead.
clips.hook_line_1: 提示词软请求vs工具硬锁
clips.hook_line_2: 彻底锁死AI乱改核心码
clips.en_title_hook: Polite Prompt Rules vs Hard Hooks
clips.summary_zh: 在提示词文档里写“禁止修改核心目录”只是礼貌请求，模型仍有概率越界；唯有在写入工具层加装前置拦截钩子，才能变成百分百铁律。
clips.en_raw: So, if you have things that are critical not to get wrong, then you need to introduce rule-based guardrails to ensure that the AI can't bypass them. To help you visualize this, imagine you have a folder called "Important, Don't Edit." You could have a rule in Claude MD that says, "Don't touch anything in the /important, don't edit folder." And that might get you 80% of the way there, but it's essentially a request, not a rule. Claude can still touch those files. So, instead, you add a pre-tool use hook before Claude uses the write or edit tool, and it checks to see the file that it's trying to edit. Now, Claude literally can't make the edit, and it's enforced at the tool level, not the prompt level. And as a result of this, this is now a concrete rule that the agent can't bypass.

To help you visualize this, imagine you have a folder called "Important, Don't Edit." You could have a rule in Claude MD that says, "Don't touch anything in the /important, don't edit folder." And that might get you 80% of the way there, but it's essentially a request, not a rule. Claude can still touch those files. So, instead, you add a pre-tool use hook before Claude uses the write or edit tool, and it checks to see the file that it's trying to edit. Now, Claude literally can't make the edit, and it's enforced at the tool level, not the prompt level. And as a result of this, this is now a concrete rule that the agent can't bypass.
clips.zh_full: 如果你手里有绝对不容出错的核心代码或配置，就必须引入基于规则的硬护栏，确保AI绝对无法绕过。举个直观例子：假设你有个文件夹，名字叫“重要机密禁止修改”。你可以在CLAUDE.md里写条规则：“绝对不要触碰这个重要文件夹里的任何内容。”这大概能帮你拦住80%的情况，但本质上这只是一句礼貌请求，而不是硬性规则——Claude依然完全有权限去改那些文件。正确做法是：在Claude调用写入或编辑工具之前，挂载前置钩子，自动检查它正准备修改的目标文件路径。一旦命中禁区，Claude在物理层面上就根本改不了！因为限制是锁死在底层工具层，而不是靠提示词自觉。如此一来，这就变成了一条刚性铁律，智能体永远不可能绕过去。

And, uh, it's just kind of an entity behind the WhatsApp. It's like a lot more understandable. Mhm. Uh, so I think to some extent it's like matching the expectations that humans already have for what an AI should behave but under the hood it's like a lot of technical details go into that. Um, I think that's like how we understand what the AI is and like the, um, description of it as Dobby or some persona obviously resonates with people.

clips.en_raw: A heist that dwarfs anything in history. Journalists, economists, and even the rare politician have warned us for decades that this level of extraction is occurring.

clips.en_raw: about things within the broad bounds of what is possible about how they use AI and how they want to be able to use AI and this is going to be a difficult question for society because there is not going to be agreement on you know, what is and isn't acceptable use of AI. clips.hook_line_1: 97软着陆vs99大崩盘
clips.hook_line_2: 收益率倒挂如何绞杀银行
clips.summary_zh: 加息一定利好银行股？华尔街策略师点破盲区：收益率曲线扁平化会严重挤压银行净息差；美联储若重演1999年对着股市猛加息，便是崩盘的开端。
clips.en_raw: All right, Liz, you suggested you think a hike's a mistake for I guess the the Main Street economy or the sort of non-financial market-dependent one. Um how would that play into the outlook for banks? Well, banks usually do well when when the Fed hikes rates, but a flatter yield curve is problematic for banks over the long term because it crimps their net interest margin. I'm not worried necessarily about what it does to the financials. I do still think that a hike would look like a mistake in hindsight. I think right now it would be a reaction to the market, not to the economy, and that's where you see the pain longer term. Now, if we want to compare it to the '90s, it depends on whether you think this is 1997 where they hiked once, 25 basis points, or this is 1999 where they kept going quite a bit and that was the beginning of the end.
